served.stem: Propylbenzene (drawn) reacts with Br2 and light (hv). Which structure is the major monobromination product?
served.bankWhy: Br2/hv is radical halogenation; the most stable radical is benzylic (resonance-stabilized into the ring), so Br goes to the benzylic carbon, giving (1-bromopropyl)benzene (option A). The internal/terminal positions are non-benzylic, and ring substitution requires FeBr3 (ionic EAS), not radical conditions.

answer.line: Light means radicals, and the benzylic radical is the most stable, so Br lands on the carbon touching the ring.

steps: Name the reaction from the reagents. Br2 with light (hv) is radical substitution: light splits Br2, and a Br atom pulls off one H.
Br takes the H that leaves the most stable radical. Pull an H from the carbon touching the ring and the radical spreads into the ring by resonance.
Br then bonds there: (1-bromopropyl)benzene. The ring stays as it is; Br on the ring needs Br2 with FeBr3.

choices.display: Br on the ring, next to the chain (ortho)
choices.note: Br on the ring comes from Br2 with FeBr3, electrophilic aromatic substitution. Light does not start that.

choices.display: Br on the end carbon of the chain
choices.note: Pulling H from the end CH3 makes a primary radical, the least stable spot on the chain.

choices.display: Br on the ring, across from the chain (para)
choices.note: The para product also needs FeBr3. With only light, the ring is left alone.
The benzylic radical is stabilized by the ring, so Br lands there.

choices.display: Br on the middle carbon of the chain
choices.note: The middle carbon gives a secondary radical. Decent, but with no resonance into the ring it loses to the benzylic one.

student.lockIt: Radical bromination puts Br at the most stable radical: benzylic or allylic, then tertiary, secondary, primary.
